newsitem.title: USA: Survivors reported on crashed Korean jet.
newsitem.headline: Survivors reported on crashed Korean jet.

text.p: Survivors are trapped in the wreckage of the Korean Air airliner which crashed in Guam early Wednesday and rescuers are having trouble reaching them, Cable News Network reported.

Citing Pentagon sources, CNN said heavy equipment was being rushed to the crashed Boeing 747 jumbo jet, which had 254 people on board. First reports said about 30 people survived the crash, and it was not immediately known how many were believed still trapped.
An airline official said that Korean Air Lines flight 801, a Boeing 747-300, was en route from Seoul when it crashed in a hilly jungle area of Guam just miles from the airport.
Airline spokesman Suh Kang-Yoon told Reuters in Seoul the plane was carrying 231 passengers and 23 crew.
Lee said Korean Air Lines Flight 801, carrying 231 passengers and 23 crew crashed into a hilly area near Guam's airport.
"Of them around 50 people were being rescued as of 5.00 a.m. (2000 GMT Tuesday). I expect the number of survivors to rise," he said without elaborating.
Lee said the Seoul government was sending a nine-member delegation to Guam to investigate the crash. They include two Foreign Ministry officials and six air transport experts.

Korean Air Lines Vice-President Lee Tae-won denied a local news report that the captain of the ill-fated aircraft told air controllers shortly before the crash that there was "something wrong" with the plane.
